abstract.text: Normalizing flows are a powerful tool for building expressive distributions in high dimensions. So far, most of the literature has concentrated on learning flows on Euclidean spaces. Some problems however, such as those involving angles, are defined on spaces with more complex geometries, such as tori or spheres. In this paper, we propose and compare expressive and numerically stable flows on such spaces. Our flows are built recursively on the dimension of the space, starting from flows on circles, closed intervals or spheres.

relations.why: The paper contrasts its direct manifold flows with the projection-based approach of Gemici et al., which can introduce singularities for non-Euclidean manifolds.

relations.quote: Here, we will show how to adapt the rational-quadratic spline flows of Durkan et al. (2019b) to satisfy the sufficient boundary conditions of circle diffeomorphisms.
relations.why: The paper builds directly on Durkan et al.'s rational-quadratic spline flows and adapts them to satisfy periodic boundary conditions for circle diffeomorphisms.

relations.quote: This is because the set of transformations Rhω, where R can be any matrix in SO(D + 1), forms a group under function composition (see Theorem 2 of Kato & McCullagh, 2015).
relations.why: The paper uses Kato & McCullagh's group-theoretic result for Möbius transformations to motivate convex combinations for increasing expressivity.

relations.quote: This motivates us to explore exponential-map flows, a mechanism for building flows on spheres proposed by Sei (2013).
relations.why: The paper adopts Sei's exponential-map flow framework and extends it with a new radial scalar field for more flexible multimodal densities.

relations.quote: Finally, a general method for defining normalizing flows on a Riemannian manifold M was proposed by Gemici et al. (2016).
relations.why: The paper critiques the Riemannian-manifold normalizing flow method for compact manifolds, where coordinate charts cannot be defined everywhere.
